newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-FLORIDA'S KEVIN BROWN THROWS FIRST NO-HITTER OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-FLORIDA'S KEVIN BROWN THROWS FIRST NO-HITTER OF YEAR.

text.p: Kevin Brown became the first pitcher in the major leagues to toss a no-hitter this season when he no hit the San Francisco Giants in Tuesday's 9-0 rout by the Florida Marlins.
Brown, who was hit hard in his last two starts, very nearly accomplished the far more rare perfect game as he retired the first 23 batters he faced.
But with two out in the eighth inning and the count at 1-2, Brown barely hit Marvin Bernard, sending him to first base to foil the perfect game bid.
Two pitches later, Mark Lewis grounded out weakly to shortstop Edgar Renteria, who flipped to second baseman Luis Castillo for the forceout to end the inning.
In the ninth, Bill Mueller grounded out to first, Stan Javier grounded out to shortstop and Brown completed the gem by striking out Darryl Hamilton looking to end the game.
He thrust his fists in the air triumphantly as his teammates raced out to congratulte him.
"I guess you're kind of on auto pilot," he said of the final out.
"You want to do the same things you've done and not start worrying about anything," added Brown, who was doused by teammates with beer and champagne in the clubhouse.
Brown threw 68 of his 99 pitches for strikes and only five pitches were clocked slower than 90 miles per hour (145 kph).

He did not allow a ball to leave the infield until Hamilton flied out to left the fourth inning. He continued mowing down Giants until the seventh, when Hamilton hit a line drive on which centre fielder Moises Alou made an over-the-shoulder catch to keep the no-hitter alive.

"He had his sinker, it was moving all over the place," said Marlins manager Jim Leyland. "You can't always see it from the dugout, but you could see it clearly today. This was a dominant no-hitter, it was not a fluke."
Brown is the second pitcher in the Florida Marlins short history to throw a no-hit game, joining Al Leiter who threw his on May 11, 1996, against the Colorado Rockies.
"This was a huge thrill," said catcher Charles Johnson, who also caught Leiter's no-hitter last year. "It's a part of history and I'll cherish it forever."
The last no-hitter in the majors came from Hideo Nomo of the Los Angeles Dodgers September 18, 1996, against Colorado.
Brown is the first pitcher to throw a no-hitter at San Francisco's Candlestick Park since Jerry Reuss accomplished the feat for the Dodgers on June 27, 1980.
"When Brown's on, he's capable of doing this," said Giants manager Dusty Baker. "He had struggled in his last three starts, so I figured he would be good today, but not this good. You feel helpless.
"The fans were into it, they were rooting for him," Baker said. "He wasn't perfect, but damned near perfect. He earned it."
